verdict.rationale: Asana's own docs confirm a native Rules feature: rule actions are offered to automate tedious work, app components can be built on rules, and a documented integration creates PagerDuty incidents from tasks "using Rules". AI Studio is described as "powerful no-code automations". However, the pack never documents how triggers and actions are configured, so the trigger-and-action builder itself is only implied. Third-party tools such as Zapier are not credited. Missing for 10: documentation of trigger types and conditions, a description of configurable action types in the rule builder, and independent or hands-on corroboration of building rules.

support.subject: As an engineer, I can build trigger-and-action automation rules to eliminate repetitive manual steps

citations.quote: Automate tedious work in powerful, bespoke ways with our platform features like rule actions, webhooks, and our API.
Build app components on the surface of tasks or rules
Automatically create PagerDuty incidents with context from Asana tasks using Rules.
